requirement: When `output.html.git-repository-url` names a GitHub repository and `output.html.edit-url-template` uses that repository's `/edit/<branch>/{path}` form, each safely resolved source location displayed for an evidence input MUST link its repository-relative file and inclusive line range to `/blob/<branch>/<file>#L<start>-L<end>`. A source location MUST remain plain text when a safe URL cannot be derived. A generated detail page MUST use its evidence JSON file as the mdBook edit target when the file exists, or its requirement chapter when the evidence file is missing.
rationale: The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.index.source_links`. **1. Link form.** - `source_links_use_configured_repository_and_branch` parses a config with `git-repository-url = https://github.com/example/project` and `edit-url-template = .../edit/release/{path}`. - It asserts `input_url("src/evidence.rs", 26, 37)` gives `https://github.com/example/project/blob/release/src/evidence.rs#L26-L37`. That checks the repository, the branch taken from the template, the file, and the inclusive `#L-L` range. - It also asserts that a path with a space and `#` is percent-encoded. - It renders a full detail page through `render_detail_page` with `source_links: Some(&links)`. The input is a real outline input whose range was computed from a file on disk (lines 26–37). The test asserts the page contains `src/evidence.rs:26–37`. - Requirement-match and definition locations go through the same `render_source_location` code, so they need no separate scenario. **2. Plain text when no safe URL can be derived.** - Unsafe or non-derivable locations are tested: `../outside.rs` and a zero start line both give `None` from `input_url`. - Configuration cases are tested too. A template for a different repository (`other/project`) gives `from_config(...) == None`. A `javascript:` repository URL and template also give `None`. - At the page level, the plain `file:start–end` form is asserted in `detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group`. That test renders with no git configuration, so no links exist, and it asserts `md/rules.md:5–7` and similar locations. The plain-text branch of `render_source_location` is the same whichever reason produced no URL. **3. Edit target.** - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` asserts that the `ready` chapter, whose evidence JSON exists, has `source_path == ../evidence/requirements.core.ready.json`. - The same test asserts that the `absent` chapter, whose evidence file is missing, has `source_path == requirements/core.md`, the requirement chapter. - `evidence_edit_path` is also checked for a nested book source directory (`docs/md` gives `../../evidence/...json`). I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept. Untested variants include a non-GitHub host, a branch name containing slashes, and a trailing slash on the repository URL. The text does not single them out beyond the cases the tests already represent: a mismatched repository and a non-GitHub scheme both resolve to `None`. The tests are marked with `{test}` references to the requirement.
